title: Beer Made from Leftover Rice Proves Popular in Japan
paragraphs: In Japan, a famous rice cooker company has found a new way to use its leftover rice: it has turned it into beer.

The company is Zojirushi, which is well known for making rice cookers and other kitchen appliances. When Zojirushi develops and tests its rice cookers, it cooks a lot of rice. In the past, this rice was used to make compost. But the company wanted to find a better use for it.

So, Zojirushi worked with Echigo Beer, a brewery in Niigata Prefecture. Echigo Beer is known as Japan's first craft beer brewery. Together, they made a beer called "Zou no Mai." In Japanese, "zou" means "elephant," which is part of Zojirushi's logo, and "mai" can mean "rice." The name also suggests that the beer is so good that it makes elephants dance.

The beer is made at Echigo Beer's factory in Nasu and is sold in 350-milliliter bottles and cans. It is a golden ale with 4.5% alcohol. It has a citrus smell and a fresh taste that is not very bitter, and it is designed to go well with Japanese food. It went on sale across Japan on March 10, 2026. Later, the company also planned to serve a version of the beer at its Zojirushi restaurants.
This is part of Zojirushi's "Rice Upcycling" project, which began in 2021. The company has also used its leftover rice to make several other products, such as wet tissues and a sweetener.
Other Japanese breweries are also making beer from leftover rice. For example, one craft brewery makes beer using cooked rice from an airport lounge buffet.
